label: The Delzant Construction
notes: Lecture 28 classified compact symplectic toric manifolds by Delzant polytopes. Today we prove surjectivity: every Delzant polytope is realized by an explicit manifold. The recipe reads the facet normals, builds a subtorus of a big torus, and reduces complex space down to the toric manifold whose moment image is the polytope.

label: Delzant Polytope Data
notes: We fix notation for the input. A Delzant polytope has d facets, each carrying a primitive inward normal vector in the integer lattice, and is cut out by the half-space inequalities pairing points against those normals. Smoothness means the normals meeting at each vertex form a lattice basis, the unimodularity condition that powers everything later.

label: The Exact Sequence of Tori
notes: The normals assemble into a surjection from the standard lattice onto the polytope lattice, sending the i-th basis vector to the i-th inward normal. Exponentiating gives a surjection of tori, and its kernel N is the subtorus we reduce by. The dual sequence transports moment maps from the big torus down to N.

label: Standard Hamiltonian Cd
notes: Complex space carries the standard symplectic form and a Hamiltonian action of the d-torus rotating each coordinate independently. Its moment map records half the squared modulus of each coordinate, shifted by the constants lambda. This single well-understood space is the universal source from which every Delzant manifold is carved by reduction.

label: Restricting to the Subtorus N
notes: Restricting the big-torus action to the subtorus N gives N a Hamiltonian action whose moment map is the dual projection composed with the standard moment map. We cut out the zero level set Z of this N-moment map. Reducing complex space by N at level zero is the heart of the construction.

label: Compactness of the Zero Level
notes: A point lies in the image of Z under the big moment map exactly when it sits in the shifted negative orthant and is killed by the dual projection. That intersection is precisely the lifted polytope, which is compact. Since the moment map is proper, the closed level set Z is compact too.

label: Faces and Vanishing Coordinates
notes: Stratify by which facet inequalities are active. A point of the quotient lands on the facet indexed by i exactly when the i-th coordinate of complex space vanishes, since the moment component equals lambda only there. Vertices force n coordinates to vanish at once, producing the largest isotropy and the toughest freeness test.

label: Freeness via Unimodularity
notes: Freeness of the N-action is checked where isotropy is worst, over vertices. There the n active normals form a lattice basis by smoothness, so the projection identifies the coordinate stabilizer torus with the full quotient torus. Its intersection with N is therefore trivial, the action is free, and the quotient is a manifold.

label: The Symplectic Quotient
notes: With N acting freely on the compact level Z, the Marsden-Weinstein quotient is a compact symplectic manifold of dimension twice n. We name it the Delzant manifold associated to the polytope. The construction is a reduction machine: feed it normals, return a smooth symplectic space of exactly the right dimension.

label: Residual Torus and Moment Image
notes: The big torus modulo N is an n-torus that descends to a Hamiltonian action on the quotient. Its moment map is induced by the standard one, and its image is exactly the polytope we started from. So the quotient is a symplectic toric manifold realizing the polytope, completing the surjectivity half of Delzant's theorem.

label: Synthesis and Example
notes: Putting it together: normals give the torus sequence, complex space supplies the universal orthant, the zero level is compact, unimodularity makes N act freely, and the quotient is toric with moment image the polytope. The standard two-simplex returns complex projective plane; replacing a normal to break smoothness breaks the manifold property exactly as predicted.
